posts.title: Voxwire
posts.description: I started Voxwire on September 14th, and today I’m open-sourcing it. It lets you talk to your computer through a throat mic: quietly, hands-free, and on your own machine. You can find it at https://github.com/66mhz/open-voxwire . MIT licensed. I built it because I wanted to be able to give commands in disguise, using internal, subvocal sounds. Subvocal speech is something I’m personally interested
i call myself `savant of ai-for-chip-design` not because i became one, because god created me this way, a very special kid in every dimension.

the speed of development in the last two years has changed drastically for me that during that time, i not only built ChipCraftX, but also built two more repositories. one is public at iOS app store, the other is online web social platform. and my rate of development is increasing exponentially every week. it is hard to play catch up if you know how to automate your flows 100%.
